column4: Some deposits from this event were carried on the top of the larger rock avalanche.
Faint long period signals are observable on O22A, S22A, RDMU, SRU, and Q24A

Volume estimate from Coe and others (2016). Initial landslide type not known. Debris flow deposits were found for this event, but the seismic signal seemed too short-lived and energetic for this event to have solely been a debris flow.

Seismic data from some of the closest stations for this event are not publicly available, including data from the North Fork Valley Seismic Network(NF) network, operated by the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) and the US Bureau of Reclamation Paradox Valley Network (RE). Data used for measurements included in this database were provided by these organizations. We do not have permission to redistribute the raw data.

Raw waveforms from closest stations. Data was demeaned but no other processing was applied. Dashed lines show approximate start and end times of event (from database). Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present.

Long period (20-60 sec) ground displacement waveforms from closest stations with detections. Dashed lines show approximate start and end times of event (from database, based on high frequency waveform). Waveforms are corrected for station response after detrending using a linear fit and tapering. Zero mean cosine filter applied with station correction may cause acausal arrivals. Figure generation is automated and there may be artifacts present. Signals with clipped waveforms and data gaps have not been removed so check raw figures before interpreting.
